clue.text: Where York and Lancaster fought in secret

definitions.meaning: the houses of York and Lancaster fought the Wars of the Roses, each under its own rose badge
sub rosa, the old Latin phrase for confidential dealings

explanation.surface: A history question about where the two medieval royal houses waged a hidden war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses (1455-87) were fought between the houses of York (white rose) and Lancaster (red rose); the phrase also translates Latin 'sub rosa', meaning confidentially.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: literally beneath the heraldic flower of either house, and idiomatically meaning confidentially, from the Latin sub rosa.

clue.text: Just out of bed. OK?

parts.note: someone who has got up is up
OK means right, correct

explanation.surface: A sleepy question asked of someone who has only just got up.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is honest and principled, which is the moral sense of upright.

clue.text: Minor set-back with the lottery

indicators.note: set back means turned round, so the word for a minor is read from its end

parts.note: a ward is a minor placed under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A small setback suffered in connection with the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like an adjective describing the set-back; it is a noun, a ward of court.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a lottery or raffle in which winners are picked at random.

clue.text: Understand how to capitalize on one's assets

definitions.meaning: to grasp or become aware of something

definitions.text: how to capitalize on one's assets
definitions.meaning: to convert property into cash, as in selling shares to raise money

explanation.surface: Advice on grasping how to make the most of what you own.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is both to grasp a fact and, in finance, to turn holdings into ready money.

clue.text: Last offer

definitions.meaning: to last is to endure or keep going
to offer something is to hold it out to someone

explanation.surface: A seller's final proposal in a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last offer' reads as a final bid; 'Last' is a verb meaning endure and 'offer' a verb meaning extend.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that hold out endure, and holding out a hand or a gift is extending it.

clue.text: Disputes cause pained expression in scientific association

indicators.note: in places the cry of pain inside the letters for the learned society

parts.note: RS stands for the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of sciences
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Quarrels among scientists make someone wince at their society's meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are noisy quarrels or arguments, so they are disputes.

clue.text: Mount the poster despite armed robbery

definitions.meaning: to put a poster up on a wall with glue or pins

explanation.surface: Someone puts up a poster even though a robbery is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a poster up on a wall, and a hold-up at gunpoint, are both expressed by this phrase.

clue.text: Get more regular teachers in one place

annotationWithheld.clue: Get more regular teachers in one place

clue.text: To climb the ladder is more satisfactory alone

parts.note: better means more satisfactory
by oneself means alone, so oneself stands for it

explanation.surface: A claim that climbing a ladder is more pleasing done solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To climb the ladder' is the social ladder, not a real one.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing the ladder is rising in status or career, which is improving your own position.

clue.text: Blissful state where Ivan ran wild

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the two names running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A happy place where a man named Ivan ran free.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the state of perfect peace and release from suffering.

clue.text: Little increase in such types of flat

parts.note: low means small in amount or height
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A small hike in what a certain kind of apartment costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is the British word for an apartment; low-rise blocks have only a few storeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-rise describes buildings of only a few floors, a common kind of apartment block.

clue.text: Hung well above ground

definitions.meaning: game meat hung until gamy and strong-smelling

explanation.surface: Something suspended far up off the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is hung until it is strong and gamy, and something far up off the earth is lofty: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Repress a lad without sex appeal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the boy surrounds the appeal

parts.note: a son is a lad, a male child
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 1920s It Girl

explanation.surface: A young man who has no allure whatsoever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' usually means lacking; here it means outside, putting IT inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on a report or a person is to suppress or squash them.

clue.text: Saint Chris provides humorous entertainment

parts.note: Kit is a pet form of Christopher, as is Chris

explanation.surface: A saint named Chris lays on a comic show.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch or parody performed for laughs.

clue.text: Be curious about why son has no work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A parent wonders why their boy has no job.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop is to pry nosily into other people's business.

clue.text: Capital has a bearing in business

indicators.note: in puts the manner inside the letters for the firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
an air is a bearing or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A capital city carries weight in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests compass direction; it means a person's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Passionate avowal of how verbs should be used?

definitions.text: avowal of how verbs should be used?
definitions.meaning: a grammarian's declaration that verbs are to be put in a tense

explanation.surface: A fervent declaration by a grammarian about correct verb usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and ardent; split as two words, the phrase says verbs belong in a tense.

clue.text: A portion kept back for every animal hunter

indicators.note: kept back here means turned round, so the word for a share is read from the end

parts.note: a part is a portion
per means for each

explanation.surface: A share of food set aside for each creature at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper catches wild creatures, usually for their fur, with snares.

clue.text: Dismissed accountant of portly frame

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
stout describes a portly, heavily built body

explanation.surface: A heavy-set accountant has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast out is to be expelled or rejected, as one dismissed is sent away.

clue.text: Flier becomes jaundiced about wife

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the yellowish word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: jaundice gives the skin a sallow, yellowish tint

explanation.surface: An airline passenger turns yellow worrying about his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an air traveller; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a fast, fork-tailed bird famed for its long migrations.

clue.text: Produce a set of clothes

definitions.meaning: to manufacture, as a factory does
an outfit, a person's dress or ...

explanation.surface: Making a complete outfit of garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory makes goods in quantity, and a smart outfit is someone's appearance: both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Quiet Spanish kingdom was model of perfection

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A peaceful Iberian realm that was held up as ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is an ideal example, someone flawless held up to imitate.

clue.text: Party leader likely to be easily influenced

indicators.note: leader here means the opening letter of the word party

parts.note: liable means likely, as in liable to happen

explanation.surface: A political head who is prone to being swayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pliable bends readily to others' wishes, as a soft material bends.

clue.text: Enterprising West Indian principal

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a head is a principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A Caribbean school head shows initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' suggests the Caribbean; it is the western Indian state of Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead firm or person is dynamic and keen to try new ventures.

clue.text: Fine language full of vivacity

indicators.note: full of says the next two words hold the answer among their letters

explanation.surface: Elegant speech brimming with liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and energetic style, a lively spirit.

clue.text: Undergarment I had put trimming on

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone sewed a decorative edge on to their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Braid is woven ornamental cord used to edge uniforms and furnishings.

clue.text: Lots of trousers

explanation.surface: A large quantity of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for plenty, and the wide-legged pants called Oxford bags.

clue.text: I stood for office in the Middle East

parts.note: to run is to stand as a candidate in an election

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have been a candidate in a Gulf country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country of the Middle East, bordering the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: A brave engineer takes note

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so the engineer's letters contain the musical note

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A courageous engineer jots something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is an old term for a Native American warrior; the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people, and a brave is a warrior of such a people.

clue.text: Sarah and Ernest love Italian port

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
Ern is a short form of Ernest
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Two people, Sarah and Ernest, adore a harbour town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a seaport city on the gulf south of Naples.

clue.text: Fish-hook 45 inches long needed by a weightlifter

parts.note: a barb is the backward point of a fish-hook, and by extension the hook
the English ell was a cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: Odd fishing tackle and a long measure required by a strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell is an obsolete cloth measure, in England 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is the long bar loaded with weights that lifters raise.

clue.text: Make excuses to jazz up the sole part

parts.note: swing is a style of jazz, so to jazz up is to swing it
taken as written
the lead is the principal or solo role in a show

explanation.surface: An actor dodges work by giving the starring role a jazzy treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: To swing the lead is British slang for shirking work by feigning illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk work with feigned illness or invented reasons is to malinger.
